title: Strict systems as modules on one ringed sequence site
statement:
Let B be a sequence of commutative ring sheaves on C. Give ℕ×C the coefficient-sequence topology whose covers are vertical C-covers at a fixed index, and the ring presheaf (n,U)↦B_n(U) with horizontal restrictions from B. This is a ring sheaf, the sequence site is essentially w-small when C is, and the category of its w-valued module sheaves is explicitly equivalent to StrictRingSystem B. Vertical module evaluation agrees with the system level functor.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w z zv t
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [EssentiallySmall.{w} C]
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
def strictSystemSequenceEquivalence : StrictRingSystem B ≌ systemSequenceModules B
```

proof.text: The existing coefficient-sequence topology describes sheaves exactly as vertically sheaf presheaves. Define the ring restrictions from B and its vertical sheaf condition levelwise. A strict system gives a module presheaf by composing horizontal semilinear transitions with vertical restrictions; the strict system laws prove functoriality and vertical sheafness gives sheafness. Conversely restrict a module sheaf vertically and obtain transitions from horizontal arrows. The coefficient ring naturality makes them linear over restriction. Unit and counit are identity maps on sections, proving the explicit equivalence and its triangles.
